recent_articles.title: Indian Air Force likely to oversee transport of NEET-UG re-test papers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The government** is considering using the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** to manage logistics and transportation for the NEET-UG 2026 re-test, scheduled for June 21.  A high-level meeting was held at the residence of **Defence Minister Rajnath Singh**, attended by **Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** and **Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia**. The IAF will provide transportation and logistics support to secure question papers from printing presses to examination centers across the country, aiming to minimize leak risks.  The final decision is pending consultations with the Prime Minister's Office.

recent_articles.title: Scorching days, restless nights: Heatwave tightens grip across parts of India - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** experienced scorching temperatures exceeding 44° Celsius in several regions, prompting **hospitals** in Punjab to activate heat stroke management units. The **IMD** issued heatwave alerts for three districts of Jharkhand and warned of rising temperatures across Delhi, Haryana, and Chandigarh.  Veterinarians and animal rescuers reported an increase in distressed birds and animals suffering from dehydration and heatstroke. In Himachal Pradesh, a yellow warning for heatwave conditions was issued for parts of the state. **Chief Ministers** of various states ordered officials to ensure adequate drinking water availability, while **Congress leader Kishori Lal Sharma** raised concerns about power supply disruptions in Uttar Pradesh's Amethi constituency.

recent_articles.title: Slow-moving bands of heavy rain trigger flooding and landslides in parts of China | China | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Heavy rainfall across southern and central China has led to flash flooding, landslides, and waterlogging. The **Bay of Bengal**, **South China Sea**, and **Pacific Ocean** contributed to the prolonged downpour that caused 12 deaths and forced evacuations.  Meanwhile, extreme heat warnings have been issued for northern India, with temperatures exceeding 40°C (104°F) in several regions. These conditions are expected to persist until Wednesday when thunderstorms may develop.

recent_articles.title: Voter confusion fears over simultaneous polls ‘misplaced’, says ONOE JPC chairman - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **P.P. Chaudhary**, chairman of the Joint Parliamentary Committee on ‘One Nation One Election’, defended the proposal, arguing that Indian voters are politically astute and can differentiate between national and state issues.  He cited examples from Delhi and other states where voters supported different parties in Lok Sabha and Assembly elections. **CII**, **ASSOCHAM**, and **GCCI** backed the proposal, while **Gujarat University Vice-Chancellor Dr. Neerja Gupta** highlighted how frequent polls disrupt academic schedules and increase financial costs. The committee also heard concerns from the **Congress**, which argued that simultaneous elections would allow national narratives to overshadow state issues.

recent_articles.title: Hockey coach Baldev Singh to be honoured with Padma Shri - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Baldev Singh**, a hockey coach who transformed the town of Shahabad Markanda into a hub for talent, will be awarded the **Padma Shri**, India's highest civilian honor.  Singh began his career in 1982 as a coach with the **Haryana Sports Department**, returning to Shahabad Markanda in 1993 and mentoring over 80 international players and eight Indian captains. He served in various roles within the competitive apparatus of hockey, including chief coach and selector for the junior men's team and assistant coach of the Indian side that won the Champions Trophy in Madras in 1996.  Singh also coached the senior national team from 2001 to 2004 and has been a key figure in shaping the institutional framework of Indian hockey.

recent_articles.title: CBI arrests ‘mastermind’ linked to NEET-UG 2026 biology paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** arrested a biology lecturer, **Manisha Gurunath Mandhare**, for her involvement in the 2026 NEET-UG paper leak case.  **Mandhare**, appointed by the **National Testing Agency (NTA)** as an expert, allegedly disclosed questions and answers from botany and zoology subjects to students through special coaching classes at her residence. The agency has arrested nine individuals in connection with the case, including a chemistry lecturer, **P.V. Kulkarni**, who allegedly leaked chemistry questions.  The CBI is conducting searches across the country and investigating leads related to the distribution of a "guess" paper that closely matched the actual exam paper.

recent_articles.title: Rajasthan seeks permanent membership in Bhakra Beas Management Board - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rajasthan** Water Resources Minister Suresh Singh Rawat called for permanent membership in the **Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB)**, arguing that Rajasthan's 52.96% share of Ravi-Beas waters necessitates representation on the board.  Rawat emphasized the need for expedited decisions regarding water storage and utilization of advanced technologies like floating solar and pumped storage power plants. He also urged for increased transparency in water distribution through real-time monitoring, automated gauging systems, and online data sharing. The call was made during a 50th anniversary celebration of the BBMB in Panchkula, Haryana, attended by Union Minister Manohar Lal Khattar, Punjab Water Resources Minister Barinder Kumar Goyal, Haryana Irrigation and Water Resources Minister Shruti Choudhary, and BBMB chairman Manoj Tripathi.

recent_articles.title: AAP, Congress raises concern over SIR in Punjab ahead of 2027 Assembly polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** issued a notification for a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Punjab and other states, prompting concerns from the **Indian National Congress** and the **Aam Aadmi Party**. The SIR exercise will involve door-to-door visits by both-level officers (BLOs) from June 25 to July 24, 2026.  The **AAP** alleged that constitutional institutions under the **BJP** rule are being misused for political advantage, while the **Congress** expressed concerns about the timing of the exercise ahead of the upcoming Punjab assembly elections. The **Haryana Chief Electoral Officer** announced a similar SIR campaign in Haryana with a qualifying date of July 1, 2026.

recent_articles.title: Lawrence Bishnoi gang stakes claim on gunfire outside Diljit Dosanjh's manager in Karnal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema** alleged that the **Lawrence Bishnoi gang** was responsible for an alleged firing incident outside the residence of Diljit Dosanjh's manager in Haryana.  **Tyson Bishnoi, Arzoo Bishnoi, and Hari Boxer**, purportedly acting on behalf of the **Bishnoi gang**, claimed responsibility for the incident via social media. **Cheema** accused the **BJP** of using gangsters to intimidate Punjabis who refuse to join their party. The **Haryana Police** have not received a complaint from the manager or his family and found no evidence at the scene.

recent_articles.title: SC asks Centre to consider States’ pleas for funds for CCTVs in police stations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** urged the **Union government** to fully implement the Assistance to States and Union Territories for Modernisation of Police (ASUMP) scheme, which provides funds for installing CCTV cameras in police stations and a centralized monitoring dashboard. The court expressed concerns over non-functional CCTV cameras in Udaipur police stations and directed the Centre to consider requests from states for funding.  The ASUMP scheme has been extended until September 30, 2026, with most states initiating steps towards compliance. However, Jharkhand was criticized for not installing any CCTV cameras, despite receiving funds under the scheme. The court also cautioned against releasing funds without due diligence to prevent misappropriation.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: TCS Nashik case: NCW flags ‘toxic work culture’, ‘zero POSH compliance’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Commission for Women (NCW)** has found that **Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)** in Nashik is failing to comply with the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act, citing pervasive harassment, religious denigration, and systemic bullying. The NCW's fact-finding committee observed that victims were intimidated into silence due to a lack of formal complaint mechanisms and a toxic workplace environment.  The committee has recommended action for TCS’ failure to comply with the POSH Act, as well as measures to protect complainants and ensure a safe working environment.

recent_articles.title: NDA leaders stake claim to form Assam government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, leader of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**-led **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)**, was unanimously elected as the leader of the Assam Legislature Party.  Following this, the NDA staked a claim to form the government in Assam with the support of 102 MLAs. The swearing-in ceremony for the new council of ministers is scheduled for May 12th. **J.P. Nadda**, Union Minister and central observer for the BJP Legislature Party meeting, announced that eight BJP legislators proposed Sarma's name as their leader.  The newly elected members of the BJP and its regional allies — **Asom Gana Parishad (AGP)** and **Bodoland People’s Front (BPF)** — chose their leaders in the morning.

recent_articles.title: CBI facilitates return of fugitive from Portugal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** facilitated the extradition of **Abhay alias Abhay Rana**, an accused wanted in multiple cases by the Haryana police, from Portugal on Saturday.  **The Ministry of External Affairs** and **the Ministry of Home Affairs** coordinated with the CBI to secure his return after he was tracked down and arrested by Portuguese authorities following an Interpol Red Notice request. A Haryana police team traveled to Portugal to take him into custody.

recent_articles.title: ED raids Punjab Minister Sanjeev Arora, linked persons again - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Directorate of Enforcement (ED)** conducted fresh searches on Saturday, May 9, 2026, targeting **Punjab Industries Minister Sanjeev Arora** and others allegedly connected to him. The raids focused on **Mr. Arora's** official residence in Chandigarh and a real estate company in Gurugram, Haryana. This action was taken under the criminal sections of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) following previous raids in April that were conducted under civil provisions of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).

recent_articles.title: Punjab worse than West Bengal under AAP rule, says Haryana CM Saini - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini** criticized the **AAP government in Punjab**, accusing it of failing to control drug trafficking, illegal mining, and lawlessness. He compared the current situation in Punjab to West Bengal under **Mamata Banerjee**, stating that people are disillusioned with the AAP and seeking change through the BJP's governance model.  Saini also contrasted the BJP's policies with those of the Congress, highlighting the latter's corruption and lack of focus on people's welfare.

recent_articles.title: Only Congress party can defeat BJP in the battle of ideologies, says Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the **Congress**, asserted that only his party could defeat the **BJP**, characterizing the upcoming election as a clash between the **RSS’s** ideology of hatred and partition and the Congress's ideology of love and unity.  He accused **Narendra Modi** of attacking India's democratic system and the Constitution, vowing that the Congress would not forget this action. **Gandhi** also criticized the U.S. trade deal, claiming it harms Indian farmers and was influenced by Mr. Modi’s "entire history" and a pending U.S. criminal case against businessman **Gautam Adani**.  The event marked a show of unity within the faction-ridden Haryana unit, with prominent Congress leaders joining him.

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: In a first, world’s smallest wild cat snapped with kitten in Faridabad; confirms breeding outside protected areas, say researchers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Researchers**, including wildlife photographer Yatin Verma, have documented the first confirmed breeding of a rusty-spotted cat in the Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) and Haryana.  The discovery was made during routine field surveys conducted since August 2022. The adult cat and its kitten were observed perched on a False Ashoka tree in Kot village, confirming active reproduction outside protected areas. This finding highlights the importance of the Aravalis mountain system for wildlife conservation, including the rusty-spotted cat, which is listed as 'Near Threatened' on the IUCN Red List.  The research paper documenting this discovery was published in Zoo’s Print.

recent_articles.title: In topsy-turvy Haryana politics, Sonipat latest amphitheatre for BJP-Cong. fight - The Hindu

The election will be decided by the votes of Punjabis, according to realtor Praveen Arora.

recent_articles.title: Independent journalism punished, compliance rewarded under current regime, says Kharge - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Saini urges Punjab OBCs to back BJP in Assembly polls - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Deepender campaigns for local polls, accuses BJP of corruption in Haryana municipal bodies - The Hindu

He accused the BJP of looting the people through corruption and highlighted specific scams in various corporations.

recent_articles.title: NIA court sentences another LeT operative in Bengaluru prison radicalisation case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The National Investigation Agency (NIA)** has convicted **Vikram Kumar alias Chota Usman**, an operative of the banned **Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT)**, in connection with the 2023 Bengaluru prison radicalisation case.  Kumar was sentenced to seven years of imprisonment and a fine of ₹30,000 for various offenses under the IPC, UAPA, and Explosive Substances Act. The court also convicted seven other accused, including **T. Naseer**, who is alleged to have orchestrated the conspiracy while in prison. Kumar was radicalized by **Naseer** and co-accused **Junaid Ahmed** during his time in Parappana Agrahara Central Prison.  The case was initially registered by the Bengaluru Central Crime Branch but was later taken over by the **NIA**, who uncovered a broader conspiracy involving prison radicalization and an escape plan for **Naseer**.

recent_articles.title: Rift widens within the Haryana BJP over its Rajya Sabha MP’s comments on former CM Bhajan Lal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kuldeep Bishnoi**, son of former Haryana Chief Minister Bhajan Lal, warned the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** against arrogance and disrespect toward senior leaders after **Rekha Sharma**, a Rajya Sabha MP, made remarks about Bhajan Lal.  Bishnoi, who joined the BJP from Congress in 2022, emphasized his contributions to the party's victories in Haryana and demanded respect for Bhajan Lal. He threatened further action if the party did not address the issue. Sharma later clarified her comments but the controversy has caused unease within the BJP.

recent_articles.title: Pioneer artist takes Swang, a folk art, to international stage - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Swang “Jaani Chor”**, a centuries-old folk theatre play from Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, has celebrated 25 years of success. Led by **Satish Georgy Kashyap**, the "King of Swang," the play's journey began in Hisar jail in 2001 and has since evolved from village chaupals to international festivals.  **Swang**, known for its blend of music, poetry, farce and dance, tells the story of a witty thief who outwits the rich and corrupt.

recent_articles.title: Planning a 15-year mutual fund investment? Here’s a simple 4-scheme portfolio approach - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ram Kumar**, a 60-year-old farmer from Haryana, is seeking to invest Rs 10 lakh in mutual funds for the next 15 years. **Srikanth Bhagavat**, MD of **Hexagon Wealth**, advises him to build a portfolio across four schemes that cover the broader Indian market and emphasizes staying invested through market volatility.  Bhagavat suggests starting with a core exposure to large-cap stocks through a Nifty index fund, followed by flexi-cap funds for additional growth potential. He recommends funds like HDFC Flexi Cap Fund, Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund, and Kotak Flexi Cap Fund as examples.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: New launches, capacity hike to lift Maruti Suzuki facing a war squeeze - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The company**, facing sales volume constraints, is expanding its capacity with two new plants in Haryana and Gujarat. The company expects an operating margin of 10% by FY30 driven by seven SUV launches and capacity expansion. Despite pressure on margins due to war-related disruptions in west Asia, the company achieved its highest-ever domestic and export volumes in FY26, aided by a GST reduction.  The company has also set targets for increasing EV presence and charging points.

recent_articles.title: ‘Harvest more water; banning paddy is not the solution to groundwater stress’ - The Hindu

Sridhar**, chairman of the State-level committee, emphasized that water used for agriculture is a resource stored for use, highlighting the importance of agriculture in the state's production. The GWRA report released on Monday advises discouraging paddy crop for Rabi season to avoid crop loss to farmers and aims to enhance groundwater recharge methods.

recent_articles.title: Haryana Assembly passes women empowerment resolution; Congress boycotts session - The Hindu

Former Chief Minister **Bhupinder Singh Hooda**, leader of the **Congress party**, accused the BJP government of making a mockery of constitutional institutions by convening the session on a matter that falls under the jurisdiction of the Central government.

recent_articles.title: World’s hottest cities: India transforms into a scorching furnace with cities shockingly hitting 46°C | World News - The Times of India

The IMD advises citizens to take precautions against heat stress by avoiding sun exposure during peak hours, staying hydrated, wearing loose-fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous activity.

recent_articles.title: 'Women will respond': Congress slams govt over 'delay' in 33% quota; says implement it at once - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: 10 of 26 petitioners caught in Russia-Ukraine crossfire dead; some volunteered, others duped, government tells Supreme Court - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: ‘Sadbhav Yatra’ has posed political challenge to BJP’s divisive politics, says Congress leader Brijendra Singh - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Govt claims women winning unreserved panchayat seats in ‘significant numbers’ - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Four feared dead in major accident on NH-50 in Karnataka’s Vijayanagara district - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Noida protests: Workers in India demand hike in minimum wage - but it's not as simple

recent_articles.title: ED searches AAP MP’s premises, linked educational institutions under FEMA - The Hindu

recent_articles.title: Former Haryana CM Hooda blames low procurement of crop on government’s “arbitrary” new rules - The Hindu
